title: Too Good to Eat Meet the Artist Who Knits Food
paragraphs: Spaghetti, pizza, ravioli and lasagne all look delicious at a new exhibition in London. But visitors should not try to eat them, because every single item is made of wool.

The food was created by Kate Jenkins, a British artist who has been knitting food for more than 30 years. Instead of using paint or clay, Jenkins uses knitting, crochet, embroidery and other textile techniques to create very realistic copies of things people eat.
Her new exhibition, called "Kate's Knitalian," is all about Italian food. It is being held at Air Contemporary, a gallery in the Soho area of London, from October 30 to December 5, 2026.

The exhibition includes bowls of spaghetti, ravioli, lasagne and pasta, as well as focaccia bread and cannoli, a type of Italian dessert. There are even knitted cans of tuna and bottles of Aperol, a popular Italian drink. Everything in the show is made from yarn or wool.
One of the most fun and popular parts of the exhibition is a pizza station. Here, visitors can build their own pizza by choosing from different crocheted toppings.

This is not the first time Jenkins has created a whole collection of knitted food. In the past, she has made a knitted ice cream shop and a knitted fish shop. Her other works include ice cream cones, bagels and plates of prawns.
All of the pieces in the London exhibition are for sale. Visitors can buy large statement pieces or smaller items to collect.

Exhibitions like this show that art does not always have to be serious. Jenkins's work makes people smile, and it also shows how much skill and patience it takes to turn simple wool into food that looks good enough to eat.
